name: Glycine

lead: Glycine is the smallest proteinogenic amino acid and makes up roughly a third of the amino acid residues in collagen. It is inexpensive, sold as a powder supplement, and is consumed in the diet through gelatin and protein foods.

In looksmaxxing and recovery circles it is used to support collagen turnover and sleep quality. Small trials suggest improved subjective sleep, but there is little direct evidence that supplementation visibly changes skin or connective tissue.

paras: Glycine acts as an inhibitory neurotransmitter in the spinal cord and brainstem and, via NMDA receptors in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, lowers core body temperature, which is the proposed route to better sleep. It is also a substrate for collagen, creatine and glutathione synthesis.

Very well tolerated at typical intakes; mild gastrointestinal upset or drowsiness can occur. It is a food-grade supplement with no particular legal restrictions. Interactions with some antipsychotics (e.g. clozapine) have been noted.
